1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
     4	# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
     5	# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
     6	# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
     7	#
     8	#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
     9	#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
    10	#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
    11	#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
    12	#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
    13	#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
    14	#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
    15	#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
    16	#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
    17	#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
    18	#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
    19	#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
    20	#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
    21	#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
    22	#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
    23	#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
    24	#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
    25	#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
    26	#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
    27	#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
    28	#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
    29	#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
    30	#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
    31	#       Run state, first match wins:
    32	#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
    33	#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
    34	#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
    35	#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
    36	#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
    37	#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
    38	#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
    39	#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
    40	#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
    41	#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
    42	#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
    43	#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
    44	#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
    45	#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
    46	#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
    47	#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
    48	#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
    49	#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
    50	#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
    51	#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
    52	#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
    53	#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
    54	#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
    55	#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
    56	#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
    57	#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
    58	#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
    59	#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
    60	#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
    61	#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
    62	#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
    63	#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
    64	#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
    65	#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
    66	#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]

   124	# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
   125	cfg() {

   187	cmd_read() {

   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)

   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}

   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
   243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
   244	impl_commit() {
   245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
   246	  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
   247	    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
   248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
   249	}

   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}

   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
   281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
   282	      .cycle += 1
   283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
   284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
   285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
   286	      | .lc = $c);
   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
   288	  {state: "CLOSED",
   289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
   290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
   291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
   292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   293	   history: []};
   294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
   295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
   297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
   298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
   299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
   300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)

   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
   229	  else
   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}

   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}

   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
   281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
   282	      .cycle += 1
   283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
   284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
   285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
   286	      | .lc = $c);
   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
   288	  {state: "CLOSED",
   289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
   290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
   291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
   292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   293	   history: []};
   294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
   295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
   297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
   298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
   299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
   300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

> # =============================================================================
> # FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
> # destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
> # pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
> # Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
> # can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
> #   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
> #   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
> # Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
> # under a caller's `set -u`.
> #
> # Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
> # to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
> # `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
> # line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
> # (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
> # tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
> # one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
> # \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
> # missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
> #   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
> #     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
> #     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
> #     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
> #     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
> #     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
> #     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
> #     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
> #     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
> #     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
> #     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
> #     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
> #     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
> #     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
> #   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
> #     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
> #     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
> #     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
> #     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
> #     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
> #     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
> #     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
> #     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
> #     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
> #     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
> #     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
> #     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
> #     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
# DEC-0141).
#
# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
# PER TASK:
#
#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
#
# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
#
# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
# file is not written through.
#
# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
#
# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
# full each time and those caches are gone.

set -uo pipefail
umask 077
export LC_ALL=C

_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
case "$switch" in
    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
esac
THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))

# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
payload="$(cat)"
[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
            else 1 end;
    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    select(type == "object") |
    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    ([($tn | tojson),
      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
       else 0 end | tostring),
      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
      (now | todate)] | .[])
' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
{
    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
    IFS= read -r LINES

        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# PreToolUse:Bash Safety Hook — Block Destructive Commands (v1.38.0)
# =============================================================================
# Blocks dangerous patterns and suggests safer alternatives.
# Exit 0 = allow, Exit 2 = block (stderr message fed back to agent).
#
# Cycle-111 (sprint-164, 2026-05-16) — ports Anthropic DCG public pattern
# set inline. Source: github.com/anthropics/destructive-command-guard
# Pattern port reference SHA: HEAD as of 2026-05-16 (no specific commit
# pin available — DCG ships rule packs, not single-file source).
# REVIEW-BY: 2026-08-16 — re-sync against upstream DCG every quarter.
#
# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — this hook must never fail closed.
# A grep or jq failure must result in exit 0 (allow), not an error.
#
# WHY fail-open (not fail-closed): A safety hook that crashes or encounters
# a parse error must NOT block the agent from operating. The alternative —
# fail-closed — would make jq/grep bugs into denial-of-service attacks
# against the agent. Fail-open with logging is the standard pattern for
# inline security hooks (cf. ModSecurity DetectionOnly mode).
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix)
#
# WHY GNU/BSD ERE (NOT strict POSIX): grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension not
# available on macOS/BSD or minimal containers. grep -E (Extended Regex)
# with `\s`, `\S`, `\b` extensions works on both GNU grep (Linux) and BSD
# grep (macOS Sonoma+). Strict-POSIX ERE (busybox without -E extensions)
# is NOT in scope per cycle-111 SDD §5.0 honest-scope decision.
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix; cycle-111 SDD §5.0)
#
# WHY single script for all patterns: NFR-5 single-file invariant. Multiple
# hooks would each read stdin, parse JSON, and run regex — multiplying
# latency per command. A single emit_block helper with sequential patterns
# is simpler and faster. (cycle-111 SDD §5/§6.)
#
# Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111 SDD §11): this hook is a fence
# against routine destructive-command mistakes by autonomous agents, NOT
# a hardened security boundary against intentional bypass. Known accepted
# bypass classes: newline statement separators, subshell wrapping
# (`bash -c '...'`, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing
# WHERE, jq absent from PATH. See SDD §11 for full table.
# Current executable limit examples and issue dispositions:
# docs/runbooks/hook-safety.md (#1047, #1245, #1088, #1031).
#
# cycle-125 FR-1 (2026-09-23) — precision pass against the fleet corpus
# (tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/, replayed by tests/unit/block-destructive-
# bash.bats). Relaxations, each on a positively established predicate:
# FR-2 cache/build vocabulary by last segment, bare names after a
# statement-initial `cd <temp>`, paths strictly below /tmp|/var/tmp|
# /private/tmp, `$TMPDIR/<name>` only with a real temp TMPDIR, a variable
# bound exactly once to `$(mktemp -d)`; FR-1.1 branches that are ancestors
# of main/master (offline `git merge-base`); FR-1.3 generated paths;
# FR-1.4/5/6 only when a SQL runner (psql, mysql, sqlite3, prisma, …) or an
# inline interpreter program (`python -c`, `node -e`) is in the command.
# ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (deliberately not relaxed):
#   * Remote payloads: `ssh host 'rm -rf /'`, `docker exec c rm -rf /data`,
#     `kubectl exec p -- rm -rf /` keep blocking. A scrub of quoted remote
#     payloads was withdrawn at design time (Flatline SKP-001) — the text
#     fence cannot tell a remote target from a local one, and the blast
#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
#
# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# jq presence probe (SDD §6.5 — SKP-008 mitigation, not full fix).
# If jq is absent, the input parse on line ~120 returns empty → existing
# fail-open guard exits 0. v1.38.0 adds a one-shot stderr WARNING so the
# operator / agent sees the safety guard is disabled this session.
# Tracked as cycle-112 candidate (filesystem-marker variant for cross-
# invocation persistence; env-var doesn't propagate across hook subprocess
# invocations per Flatline SKP-002 round-3 finding).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-11 (skill-loop, 2026-07-06): HIGH-002 fix (BB review of PR #1176).
# Passes 2 & 8 introduced bash-4-only constructs into this fence (${x,,}
# case-folding, `mapfile`); pre-loop it was bash-3.2-portable (echo|grep -i).
# macOS ships bash 3.2. This guard runs BEFORE any bash-4 expansion executes
# (bash 3.2 defers ${,,} validation and the mapfile builtin lookup to runtime,
# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)
# and argv survive exec. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED (exit 2 = block): a
# destructive-command fence must never silently allow when it cannot evaluate.
# The generic bash-version-guard.sh exits 1, which is a NON-blocking PreToolUse
# hook error (fail-OPEN) — wrong direction for this hook, hence the inline form.
if [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -lt 4 ]; then
    for _bh_cand in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/bash /usr/bin/bash bash; do
        if command -v "$_bh_cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            _bh_major="$("$_bh_cand" -c 'echo "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}"' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
            if [ "${_bh_major:-0}" -ge 4 ]; then exec "$_bh_cand" "$0" "$@"; fi
        fi
    done
    echo "[block-destructive-bash] BLOCKED: bash >=4 required to evaluate the destructive-command fence (found ${BASH_VERSION:-unknown}); refusing to run degraded rather than allow a command unchecked. Install bash>=4 (macOS: brew install bash)." >&2
    exit 2
fi

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [[ -z "${LOA_BLOCK_DESTRUCTIVE_JQ_MISSING_WARNED:-}" ]]; then
    echo "WARNING: block-destructive-bash: jq not in PATH — destructive-command pattern matching is DISABLED for this session. Install jq to restore safety guards." >&2
    export LOA_BLOCK_DESTRUCTIVE_JQ_MISSING_WARNED=1
  fi
  exit 0  # Existing fail-open behavior preserved.
fi

# perf pass-2: pin byte-oriented ASCII regex/case-fold semantics for both the
# remaining greps and the bash [[ =~ ]]/${var,,} conversions. All patterns in
# this file are pure-ASCII; C-locale folding is the semantics they were
# written for (and what the test/golden harness already pins).
export LC_ALL=C

# Read tool input from stdin (JSON with tool_input.command).
# Path A jq call (SDD §6.4): failure here → empty $command → allow.
# perf pass-2: jq reads the hook's stdin directly — identical bytes reach the
# same jq program; the interim $(cat) copy and echo-pipe only added 2 forks.
command=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true

# If we can't parse the command, allow (don't block on parse errors).
if [[ -z "$command" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# quote-blindness scrub (bd-bdb-quote-blindness-pt1g).
# Produce _cmd_match, a LOCAL scrub-copy of $command used SOLELY for the
# block/allow decision below. $command itself is left byte-for-byte intact so
# emit_block's audit row still records the operator's original command.
#
# The fence is quote-blind: it sees a destructive TOKEN (rm -rf, DROP/TRUNCATE
# TABLE, DELETE FROM, git branch -D, ...) inside an INERT data carrier — an
# echo argument, a git commit message, a bead description, a gh PR body — and
# blocks a harmless command. The GENERAL problem (deciding whether an arbitrary
# quoted string will be executed) is NOT tractable in a regex fence — any
# allowlist of *execution* shapes (ssh/su -c/sh -c/xargs/...) is unbounded and
# reintroduces bypass (issue #1047). This is the INVERSE: a curated allowlist
# of KNOWN-INERT data carriers, whose value we redact into the scrub-copy.
#
# The metadata content gate (cycle-120 C-D3a) leaves values containing `$(` or
# backticks INTACT, including `$$(...)`. Those expansions can execute even in
# double quotes. A lone `$` is permitted. Double-quote escapes are consumed as
# pairs so an escaped quote cannot open a fake tail flag spanning a live write.
# The command-position prefix check rejects names inside other quoted data or
# interpreter/eval arguments. Unknown contexts retain conservative matching;
# these bounded recognizers do not establish arbitrary execution semantics.
#
# Carrier values may contain literal separators; following executable segments
# remain visible, so `echo 'safe' && rm -rf /` still blocks. Word boundaries and
# the prefix check keep `notgit commit -m '…'` from matching. echo/printf stays a sed
# scrub (rest-of-segment, not a quoted value); the git/br/gh quoted-value
# carriers use the content-gated bash loop `_bdb_scrub` below (replace the value
# with a single SPACE, never empty). BSD/GNU ERE only — no \b (BSD libc lacks
# it; header §).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bare echo/printf carrier: from a segment-start echo/printf to the end of its
# segment. The rest-class excludes ; & | (segment separators — per-segment
# scoping), $ and backtick (command-substitution — never redact past them), and
# < > (redirect operators — leave redirects + their targets intact so the FR-SZ
# State-Zone write guard, which keys off the raw path, still fires on
# `echo x >> .run/cron.d/job.sh`).
_bdb_sed_echo='s/(^|;|&&|\|\||\|)([[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?(echo|printf)[[:space:]]+)[^;&|<>$`]*/\1\2 /g'

# Quoted-value carriers (git commit -m / br|bd … -d / gh … create --body|--title).
# cycle-120 C-D3a: content-gated redaction. The value permits `$` and stops at
# an unescaped closing quote; _bdb_scrub then applies the content gate. The
# quoted value is the penultimate capture group. [^;&|]* keeps
# the prefix within one segment; (^|[^[:alnum:]_]) is the anti-spoof boundary.
# cycle-120 R1 fix (CRITICAL): the pre-flag prefix classes ALSO exclude quotes
# (`[^;&|'"]*`). Without that, POSIX leftmost-longest lets the prefix walk PAST
# the real flag+opening-quote and re-anchor on a decoy flag literal embedded in
# the value (`git commit -m "-m " && rm -rf "/"`), so the value capture spans
# from the string's real closing quote to the NEXT quote — swallowing a live
# `&& rm -rf "` into a redacted "carrier value". Barring quotes from the prefix
# means a flag can only be matched before any quote in the segment is opened.
# A double-quoted value consumes backslash/character pairs together. An escaped
# quote must never become a terminator and expose a fake subsequent flag.
# The value is the penultimate group; the last group is the double-quote atom.
_bdb_qval_perm="('[^']*'|\"([^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\")"
_bdb_re_git="(^|[^[:alnum:]_])git[[:space:]][^;&|'\"]*commit[^;&|'\"]*(-m|--message)[[:space:]]+${_bdb_qval_perm}"
_bdb_re_brbd="(^|[^[:alnum:]_])(br|bd)[[:space:]][^;&|'\"]*(create|update)[^;&|'\"]*(-d|--description)[[:space:]]+${_bdb_qval_perm}"
_bdb_re_gh="(^|[^[:alnum:]_])gh[[:space:]][^;&|'\"]*(issue|pr)[^;&|'\"]*create[^;&|'\"]*(--body|--title)[[:space:]]+${_bdb_qval_perm}"
# cycle-125 FR-1 (D-1.7): the quoted pattern argument of a read-only search
# tool is text, never a command — `grep -rn "rm -rf dist" file` and
# `rg 'DROP TABLE' migrations/` were the most common benign shapes the SQL and
# rm rules matched. Only grep-family tools are carriers here: sed/awk can
# execute (`s///e`, `system()`), so their scripts stay visible. The value is
# the first quoted argument after any flags; content-gated like every carrier.
_bdb_re_grep="(^|[^[:alnum:]_])(grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|ag|ack)[[:space:]]+((-[^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+)*${_bdb_qval_perm}"

# Tail-run of contiguous message flags after the primary carrier match. A
# single `git commit`/`gh create`/… can carry MULTIPLE `-m/--message`/`-d`/
# `--body`… pairs (git concatenates multi-`-m` into paragraphs). The primary
# regex, now that the prefix bars quotes (R1 fix), only anchors the FIRST pair;
# this tail consumes further contiguous `flag <quoted-value>` pairs so all of a
# genuine multi-flag message is redacted. It is anchored at the START of the
# remaining text (`^[[:space:]]*flag …`), so it CANNOT cross a statement
# separator: the moment the remainder begins with anything other than another
# message flag (e.g. `&& rm -rf`), the tail stops and that text is left INTACT
# for FR-2. This keeps multi-`-m` benign commits allowed WITHOUT reopening the
# `&&`-crossing bypass.
_bdb_re_tail="^[[:space:]]*(-m|--message|-d|--description|--body|--title)[[:space:]]+${_bdb_qval_perm}"

# A carrier name must start a command, not occur inside another value or an
# interpreter/eval argument. This small prefix scan tracks quoting/escaping
# only; complex substitution/heredoc prefixes are conservatively left raw.
_bdb_at_command_start() {
  local prefix="$1" i ch quote="" escaped=0 at_start=1
  [[ "$prefix" != *'$('* && "$prefix" != *'`'* && "$prefix" != *'<<'* ]] || return 1
  for ((i=0; i<${#prefix}; i++)); do
    ch="${prefix:i:1}"
    if [[ "$quote" == "'" ]]; then
      [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && quote=""
      continue
    fi
    if (( escaped )); then escaped=0; at_start=0; continue; fi
    if [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then escaped=1; at_start=0; continue; fi
    if [[ "$quote" == '"' ]]; then
      [[ "$ch" == '"' ]] && quote=""
      continue
    fi
    case "$ch" in
      "'"|'"') quote="$ch"; at_start=0 ;;
      '#') return 1 ;;
      ';'|'&'|'|'|$'\n') at_start=1 ;;
      ' '|$'\t') ;;
      *) at_start=0 ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ -z "$quote" && "$escaped" == 0 && "$at_start" == 1 ]]
}

# _bdb_scrub <carrier-ere> <input> — echo the input with every carrier value
# that passes the content gate replaced by a single SPACE (never empty, never
# crossing a segment). A value containing `$(` (this catches `$$(` too — the
# substring is present) or a backtick is left INTACT. bash =~ exposes no match
# offset, so the split is by string slice on the matched text.
_bdb_scrub() {
  local re="$1" rest="$2" out="" m val inner pre po vi boundary
  while [[ "$rest" =~ $re ]]; do
    m="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
    boundary="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    vi=$(( ${#BASH_REMATCH[@]} - 2 ))   # group before the double-quote atom
    val="${BASH_REMATCH[$vi]}"
    pre="${rest%%"$m"*}"                 # text before this match
    rest="${rest#*"$m"}"                 # text after this match
    if ! _bdb_at_command_start "$out$pre$boundary"; then
      out+="$pre$m"
      continue                         # no tail recovery inside unknown quoting
    fi
    inner="${val:1:${#val}-2}"          # strip the outer quotes
    if [[ "$inner" == *'$('* || "$inner" == *'`'* ]]; then
      out+="$pre$m"                     # command-sub value — leave INTACT
    else
      po="${m%"$val"}"                  # matched text minus the trailing value
      out+="$pre$po "                   # value → single space
    fi
    # Consume any contiguous trailing message-flag pairs (multi-`-m`), each
    # content-gated the same way. Stops at the first non-flag token (separator
    # or real content), so it never crosses a statement boundary.
    while [[ "$rest" =~ $_bdb_re_tail ]]; do
      m="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
      vi=$(( ${#BASH_REMATCH[@]} - 2 ))
      val="${BASH_REMATCH[$vi]}"
      rest="${rest#"$m"}"
      inner="${val:1:${#val}-2}"
      if [[ "$inner" == *'$('* || "$inner" == *'`'* ]]; then
        out+="$m"                       # command-sub value — leave INTACT
      else
        po="${m%"$val"}"
        out+="$po "
      fi
    done
  done
  printf '%s' "$out$rest"
}

# #1245: recognize ONLY a complete, standalone cat with a quoted heredoc.
# The delimiter disables shell expansion in the body. The header remains
# visible (including protected redirect targets). Interpreter consumers,
# pipelines, unquoted delimiters, nested contexts and trailing commands keep
# their raw text: the body may execute in those forms. This is deliberately
# a small carrier grammar, not a shell parser.
_bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc() {
  local text="$1" header rest marker delim strip_tabs line candidate
  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
  [[ "$text" == *$'\n'* ]] || { printf '%s' "$text"; return; }
  header="${text%%$'\n'*}"
  if [[ ! "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$text"; return
  fi
  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
  strip_tabs="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  delim="${BASH_REMATCH[3]:-${BASH_REMATCH[4]}}"
  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
  if [[ ! "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$text"; return
  fi
  rest="${text#*$'\n'}"
  while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
    line="${rest%%$'\n'*}"
    if [[ "$rest" == *$'\n'* ]]; then rest="${rest#*$'\n'}"; else rest=""; fi
    if [[ "$strip_tabs" == "-" ]]; then
      while [[ "$line" == $'\t'* ]]; do line="${line#$'\t'}"; done
    fi
    if [[ "$line" == "$delim" ]]; then
      if [[ -z "$rest" ]]; then printf '%s' "$header"; else printf '%s' "$text"; fi
      return
    fi
  done
  # No closing delimiter: leave the entire command visible.
  printf '%s' "$text"
}

# #1245: two COMPLETE data-only programs, not arbitrary interpreter exemptions.
# Loop: single-quoted items, one printf with a fixed format and the same lower-
# case variable. Python: single-quoted -c source, double-quoted string literals
# without escapes, a list optionally assigned and printed. No imports, calls
# other than that print, interpolation, other consumers or trailing shell text.
# Single shell quotes keep $()/backticks in these literals inert. Any mismatch
# retains raw input, including double-quoted arguments where expansions execute.
_bdb_scrub_literal_program() {
  local text="$1" loop_re python_re source name list_re program_re
  loop_re="^[[:space:]]*for[[:blank:]]+([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)[[:blank:]]+in[[:blank:]]+'[^']*'([[:blank:]]+'[^']*')*[[:blank:]]*;[[:space:]]*do[[:space:]]+printf[[:blank:]]+'%s"
  loop_re+='\\n'
  loop_re+="'[[:blank:]]+"
  loop_re+='"[$]([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)"[[:blank:]]*;[[:space:]]*done[[:space:]]*$'
  if [[ "$text" =~ $loop_re ]] && [[ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" == "${BASH_REMATCH[3]}" ]]; then
    printf '%s' ': literal loop data'
    return
  fi
  python_re="^[[:blank:]]*python3?[[:blank:]]+-c[[:blank:]]+'([^']*)'[[:blank:]]*$"
  if [[ "$text" =~ $python_re ]]; then
    source="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    list_re='\[[[:space:]]*("[^"\\]*"[[:space:]]*(,[[:space:]]*"[^"\\]*"[[:space:]]*)*,?[[:space:]]*)?\]'
    program_re="^[[:space:]]*${list_re}[[:space:]]*$"
    if [[ "$source" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*= ]]; then
      name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      program_re="^[[:space:]]*${name}[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*${list_re}([[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*print\([[:space:]]*${name}[[:space:]]*\))?[[:space:]]*$"
    fi
    if [[ "$source" =~ $program_re ]]; then
      printf '%s' ': literal Python data'
      return
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s' "$text"
}

# Heredoc scrub, then quoted-value carriers, then echo/printf (sed).
# The echo scrub must run last: it can otherwise consume a closing quote in
# metadata containing "; echo ..." and make a later live write look quoted.
# (bash loops, each guarded by a cheap literal test so the benign path pays
# nothing beyond the substring check).
_cmd_match="$command"
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"for "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"python"* ]]; then
  _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_literal_program "$_cmd_match")
fi
# cycle-129 FR-6: with destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier on (the
# default) the fail-closed consumer classifier above replaces the #1245 scrub,
# which survives unchanged as its special case and as the knob-off path.
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"<<"* ]]; then
  if _bdb_heredoc_knob_on; then
    _cmd_match=$(_bdb_heredoc_scrub "$_cmd_match")
  else
    _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc "$_cmd_match")
  fi
fi
[[ "$_cmd_match" == *"git"* ]] && _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_git" "$_cmd_match")
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"br "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"bd "* ]]; then
  _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_brbd" "$_cmd_match")
fi
[[ "$_cmd_match" == *"gh "* ]] && _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_gh" "$_cmd_match")
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *grep* || "$_cmd_match" == *"rg "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"ag "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"ack "* ]]; then
  _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_grep" "$_cmd_match")   # cycle-125 D-1.7
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
#
# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
# unless stated):
#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
#
# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
#
# Inputs (each has a test seam):
#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
#
# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
# =============================================================================

_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
_LOA_PL_JSON=""
_LOA_PL_ID=""

_loa_pl_paths() {
  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
  else
    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
  fi
}

# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
_loa_pl_id() {
  local st
  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    return 0
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
}

_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
_loa_pl_build() {
  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
      cfg='{}'
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
      prof='{}'
    fi
  else
    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
  fi
  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
        else . end)) as $knobs |
    {
      schema_version: 1,
      id: $id,
      profile: $sel.name,
      profile_source: $sel.source,
      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
      profile_keys: $keys,
      knobs: $knobs,
      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
  local w
  while IFS= read -r w; do
    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
  return 0
}

_loa_pl_write_cache() {
  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  fi
  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  else
    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  fi
  return 0
}

# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
_loa_pl_load() {
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
    local j
    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  _loa_pl_build || return 1
  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
  _loa_pl_write_cache
  return 0
}

# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
_loa_pl_live() {
  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else
    echo default
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_overrides() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_effective_json() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
  else
    echo '{}'
  fi
  return 0
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
  export LC_ALL=C
  case "${1:-}" in
    profile)   loa_profile ;;
    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi

The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
> 
> - **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
> - **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
> - **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. #!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}

@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
    write_lines 3
    write_lines 2
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb
    write_lines 2
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-bbb" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.over' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl")" -eq 2 ]
    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-bbb.jsonl")" -eq 1 ]
    [ "$(tail -1 "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl" | jq -r '.running_total')" = "5" ]
}

@test "KS-2 with no run in progress the key is the payload's session id, then LOA_SESSION_ID" {
    write_lines 1 "abc-123"
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/abc-123.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "abc-123" ]
    jq -nc '{tool_name: "Edit", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/a", old_string: "", new_string: "x\ny"}}' \
        | LOA_SESSION_ID=env-sess bash "$HOOK"
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/env-sess.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
}

@test "KS-3 a checkpoint whose task is still open in beads keys on the sprint" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-open
    BR_STATUS=open write_lines 2
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/sprint-256.jsonl" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-open.jsonl" ]
    # A sprint-granularity checkpoint (no task) keys on the sprint too.
    checkpoint sprint-257
    write_lines 1
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "sprint-257" ]
}

@test "KS-4 the summary carries exactly task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at after each write" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sum
    write_lines 4
    run jq -c 'keys' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE"
    [ "$output" = '["lines","over","task","threshold","updated_at"]' ]
    jq -e '.task == "bd-sum" and .lines == 4 and .threshold == 5 and .over == false
           and (.updated_at | test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}Z$"))' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 3
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    jq -e '.lines == 7 and .over == true' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
    # The stderr warning keeps its wording.
    [[ "$stderr" == "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total 7 lines exceeds threshold 5. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-sum.jsonl" ]]
    ls "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE".tmp.* >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
    true
}

@test "KS-5 the state directory keeps the 20 most recently written task files" {
    mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
    local i
    for i in $(seq -w 1 25); do
        echo '{"lines_changed":1}' > "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
        touch -d "2026-01-01 00:00:$i" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
    done
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-new
    write_lines 1
    [ "$(ls "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl | wc -l)" -eq 20 ]
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-new.jsonl" ]
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-25.jsonl" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-06.jsonl" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-01.jsonl" ]
}

@test "KS-6 the legacy session-long state file is deleted on the first run" {
    printf '{"lines_changed":900,"running_total":900}\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-leg
    write_lines 1
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE" ]
    # The legacy total does not leak into the new layout.
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "1" ]
}

@test "KS-7 task names are sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\$ and stay inside the state directory" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 'bd-1'
    jq '.checkpoint.task = "Task 2.3: ../../evil\nname"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    write_lines 1
    run ls -A "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
    [ "${#lines[@]}" -eq 1 ]
    [[ "${lines[0]}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.jsonl$ ]]
    [ "${lines[0]}" = "Task_2.3__.._.._evil_name.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(find "$T" -name '*evil*' | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]
    # A leading dot cannot make a hidden (unrotated) file.
    jq '.checkpoint.task = ".hidden"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    write_lines 1
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/_hidden.jsonl" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "_hidden" ]
}

@test "KS-8 knob off is silent: no state, no summary, no stderr" {
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: false\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    printf 'x\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
    # The `lean` profile turns it off without the key; an explicit true wins over lean.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
    [ -z "$stderr" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
    [[ "$stderr" == *"[karpathy-surgical-warn]"* ]]
}

@test "KS-9 content never reaches state, summary or trajectory" {
    local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sec
    jq -nc --arg c "a
$secret
b
c
d
e" '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: "s", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/x", content: $c}}' | bash "$HOOK" 2>/dev/null
    ! grep -rqF "$secret" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR"
    [ -f "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR/karpathy-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d).jsonl" ]
}

@test "KS-10 a symlinked state directory or task file is not written through" {
    mkdir -p "$T/elsewhere"
    ln -s "$T/elsewhere" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-link
    write_lines 1
    [ -z "$(ls -A "$T/elsewhere")" ]
    rm "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"; mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
    ln -s "$T/elsewhere/target" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-link.jsonl"
    write_lines 1
    [ ! -e "$T/elsewhere/target" ]
}

@test "KS-11 malformed or foreign payloads are a silent no-op" {
    run bash -c "printf 'not json' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run bash -c "printf '%s' '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"ls\"}}' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run bash -c "printf '%s' '[1,2]' | '$HOOK'"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ]
}
