#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh — byte budgets for the always-loaded prompt surface
#
# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1). The prompt surface Claude loads on every turn or on
# every skill invocation has hard byte budgets; this is the CI gate behind them.
#
#   .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md      ≤ 16,384 B  each — charged with every
#                                  resources/*.md the skill reads UNCONDITIONALLY
#   .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      ≤ 9,445 B (cycle-129 D-3.3: min(previous cap, measured 9,189 B + 256 B); the cap never rises)
#   .claude/protocols/*.md (total) ≤ 160,000 B fail; > 114,688 B warns (reference/ is not counted)
#
# Resource charging rule (the byte budget cannot be met by moving text into a
# file the skill still always loads): a resources/<name>.md is charged when a
# SKILL.md line names it AND reads as an unguarded read imperative —
#   imperative: (?i)\b(read|load|source|include)\b          e.g. "Read `resources/X.md`"
#   guard:      (?i)\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b
# A line with a guard word ("See resources/X.md §Security", "read X.md if …") is
# a pointer, not a load, and is not charged. Pinned by tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats.
#
# Every other SKILL.md figure the sprint report needs from the "mechanical pass"
# (history tokens per file) rides along in --json as `history_tokens` —
# informational; enforcement of that rule is tests/unit/no-history-in-rule-text.bats.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh              # human table, exit 1 on any breach
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json       # machine-readable report
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root DIR   # check a fixture tree (tests / CI sentinels)
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --quiet      # exit code only
#
# Exit codes: 0 within budget · 1 breach · 2 usage / missing root
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

ROOT="."
JSON=0
QUIET=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    --quiet|-q) QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[[ -d "$ROOT/.claude" ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: no .claude/ under $ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }

python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$JSON" "$QUIET" <<'PY'
import glob, json, os, re, sys
root, as_json, quiet = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] == "1", sys.argv[3] == "1"
SKILL_LIMIT, LOA_LIMIT, PROTO_FAIL, PROTO_WARN = 16384, 9445, 160000, 114688
IMPERATIVE = re.compile(r"\b(read|load|source|include)\b", re.I)
GUARD = re.compile(r"\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b", re.I)
HISTORY = re.compile(r"cycle-[0-9]{3}|#[0-9]{3,4}|KF-[0-9]{3}")
RES = re.compile(r"resources/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.md)")

def size(p):
    return os.path.getsize(p)

violations, skills = [], []
for skill_md in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, ".claude/skills/*/SKILL.md"))):
    sdir = os.path.dirname(skill_md)
    name = os.path.basename(sdir)
    charged, seen = [], set()
    text = open(skill_md, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    for ln, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        for m in RES.finditer(line):
            rel = m.group(1)
            if rel in seen or not IMPERATIVE.search(line) or GUARD.search(line):
                continue
            rp = os.path.join(sdir, "resources", rel)
            if os.path.isfile(rp):
                seen.add(rel)
                charged.append({"path": os.path.relpath(rp, root), "bytes": size(rp), "line": ln})
    total = size(skill_md) + sum(c["bytes"] for c in charged)
    ok = total <= SKILL_LIMIT
    skills.append({"skill": name, "path": os.path.relpath(skill_md, root), "skill_md_bytes": size(skill_md),
                   "charged_resources": charged, "total": total, "limit": SKILL_LIMIT, "ok": ok,
                   "history_tokens": len(HISTORY.findall(text))})
    if not ok:
        extra = f" (+{len(charged)} charged resource(s))" if charged else ""
        violations.append(f"skill {name}: {total} B > {SKILL_LIMIT} B{extra}")

loa_path = os.path.join(root, ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md")
loa = {"path": ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md", "bytes": size(loa_path) if os.path.isfile(loa_path) else 0,
       "limit": LOA_LIMIT, "present": os.path.isfile(loa_path)}
loa["ok"] = loa["bytes"] <= LOA_LIMIT
if not loa["ok"]:
    violations.append(f"CLAUDE.loa.md: {loa['bytes']} B > {LOA_LIMIT} B")

pfiles = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, ".claude/protocols/*.md")))
protos = [{"path": os.path.relpath(p, root), "bytes": size(p)} for p in pfiles]
ptotal = sum(p["bytes"] for p in protos)
protocols = {"total": ptotal, "count": len(protos), "fail_limit": PROTO_FAIL, "warn_limit": PROTO_WARN,
             "ok": ptotal <= PROTO_FAIL, "warn": PROTO_WARN < ptotal <= PROTO_FAIL, "files": protos}
if not protocols["ok"]:
    violations.append(f"protocols total: {ptotal} B > {PROTO_FAIL} B")

report = {"ok": not violations, "skills": skills, "claude_loa": loa, "protocols": protocols, "violations": violations}
if as_json:
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
elif not quiet:
    print(f"{'skill':<32}{'SKILL.md':>10}{'charged':>10}{'total':>10}  limit {SKILL_LIMIT}")
    for s in skills:
        flag = "" if s["ok"] else "  BREACH"
        print(f"{s['skill']:<32}{s['skill_md_bytes']:>10}{sum(c['bytes'] for c in s['charged_resources']):>10}{s['total']:>10}{flag}")
    print(f"CLAUDE.loa.md {loa['bytes']} B (limit {LOA_LIMIT}){'' if loa['ok'] else '  BREACH'}")
    pw = "  WARN (> %d)" % PROTO_WARN if protocols["warn"] else ("" if protocols["ok"] else "  BREACH")
    print(f"protocols total {ptotal} B over {len(protos)} files (fail > {PROTO_FAIL}){pw}")
if violations and not quiet and not as_json:
    print("\nBUDGET BREACH:", file=sys.stderr)
    for v in violations:
        print("  " + v, file=sys.stderr)
elif protocols["warn"] and not quiet and not as_json:
    print(f"WARN: protocols total {ptotal} B exceeds the {PROTO_WARN} B warning threshold", file=sys.stderr)
sys.exit(1 if violations else 0)
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

cmd_record_round() {
  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  local p th ts now out trip
  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
    return 0
  fi
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
        else null end ) as $trip
    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
  echo "$out"
  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
    return 10
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_mark() {
  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    local err drc=0
    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  fi
  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
}

case "$sub" in
  write)  cmd_write ;;
  read)   cmd_read ;;
  derive) cmd_derive ;;
  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac

# --- Capability-to-tool mapping (SDD §3.3) ---
# Returns 0 if tool is in allowed-tools
has_tool() {
    local allowed="$1" tool="$2"
    # Use word-boundary matching to prevent substring false positives
    # (e.g., "WriteConfig" should not match "Write")
    echo "$allowed" | grep -qiwF "$tool"

# # ICM-L2-INPUTS-LINT: ICM Layer-2 advisory inputs manifest rot-lint.
# Reads the optional top-level `inputs:` frontmatter list (each entry: path[, why]).
# For each DECLARED path, WARNs (advisory only) if it is absent on disk — a drift
# signal that the skill's known-failures-first / context inputs have moved. It NEVER
# flags an undeclared read and NEVER fails the build. Absence of a manifest is fine.
validate_skill_inputs() {
    local skill_name="$1" frontmatter="$2"
    local inputs_raw n i p
    inputs_raw=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.inputs' - 2>/dev/null) || inputs_raw="null"
    [[ "$inputs_raw" == "null" || -z "$inputs_raw" ]] && return 0
    local itype; itype=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.inputs | type' - 2>/dev/null) || itype=""
    [[ "$itype" == "!!seq" ]] || { log_advisory "$skill_name" "inputs: is not a list (manifest ignored)"; return 0; }
    n=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.inputs | length' - 2>/dev/null) || n=0
    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    for ((i=0; i<n; i++)); do
        p=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval ".inputs[$i].path // \"\"" - 2>/dev/null) || p=""
        if [[ -z "$p" ]]; then
            log_advisory "$skill_name" "inputs[$i] declares no 'path' (advisory manifest entry ignored)"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ "$p" == *'*'* ]]; then
            compgen -G "$PROJECT_ROOT/$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || log_advisory "$skill_name" "declared input not found on disk (drift): $p"
        else
            [[ -e "$PROJECT_ROOT/$p" ]] || log_advisory "$skill_name" "declared input not found on disk (drift): $p"
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
#
# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
# unless stated):
#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
#
# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
#
# Inputs (each has a test seam):
#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
#
# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
  _loa_pl_write_cache
  return 0
}

# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
_loa_pl_live() {
  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else
    echo default
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_overrides() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_effective_json() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
  else
    echo '{}'
  fi
  return 0
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
  export LC_ALL=C
  case "${1:-}" in
    profile)   loa_profile ;;
    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
#
# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
#
# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
#
# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
schema_version: 1

profiles:
  lean:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: false
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: false
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  standard:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  full:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: true
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: true
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: true

+  fi
+  return 0
+}

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.

file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
# DEC-0141).
#
# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
# PER TASK:
#
#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
#
# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
#
# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
# file is not written through.
#
# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
#
# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
# full each time and those caches are gone.

set -uo pipefail
umask 077
export LC_ALL=C

_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
case "$switch" in
    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
esac
THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))

# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
payload="$(cat)"
[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
            else 1 end;
    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    select(type == "object") |
    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    ([($tn | tojson),
      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
       else 0 end | tostring),
      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
      (now | todate)] | .[])
' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
{
    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
    IFS= read -r LINES
    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
    IFS= read -r TS
} <<< "$fields"
case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
    *) exit 0 ;;
esac
[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0

# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
    local s
    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
#
# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
    for p in lean standard; do
        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
    done
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
}

# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }

@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
    local pin actual
    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
}

@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
import re, subprocess, sys, json
def load(p):
    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
assert len(keys) == 9, keys
bad = []
for k in keys:
    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
            bad.append((k, f))
print("violations:", bad)
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
PY
    echo "$output"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
}

@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
    local p k
    for p in lean standard; do
        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
    done
    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
def walk(x, path):
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        for k, v in x.items():
            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
    if path:
        key = ".".join(path)
        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
            out.add(key)
for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
PY
    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
    for g in code_review security_audit; do
        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
    done
}

@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
    local f p
    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
    for f in ok bad; do
        for p in lean standard; do
            rc=0
            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
        done
        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
    done
    # The fixtures exercise both outcomes, so identity is not vacuous.
    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
}

@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
    mkdir -p "$d"
    for p in lean standard; do
        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
        rc=0
        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
    done
    cmp "$T/gate-lean.out" "$T/gate-standard.out"
    # No dissent envelope for an enabled gate: the gate refuses (exit 2) under both.
    [ "$(tail -1 "$T/gate-lean.out")" = "2" ]
    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"
    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qi 'adversarial'
}

@test "PF-6 the fence decides every corpus row and the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes identically under lean and standard" {
    local p row cmd rc id
    jq -r '.id' "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" > /dev/null
    # Floor probes (the corpus carries the floor rules named in floor.yaml floor_corpus when they exist).
    printf '%s\n' \
        '{"id":"FP-1","cmd":"git stash pop 2>/dev/null"}' \
        '{"id":"FP-2","cmd":"git stash push -m x | tail -1"}' \
        '{"id":"FP-3","cmd":"echo x > .claude/hooks/evil.sh"}' \
        '{"id":"FP-4","cmd":"cp /tmp/a .claude/settings.json"}' \
        '{"id":"FP-5","cmd":"sed -i s/a/b/ .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"}' > "$T/probes.jsonl"
    cat "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" "$T/probes.jsonl" > "$T/all.jsonl"
    for p in lean standard; do
        mkdir -p "$T/root-$p/repo"
        cp "$T/$p.yaml" "$T/root-$p/.loa.config.yaml"
        : > "$T/fence-$p.txt"
        while IFS= read -r row; do
            [ -n "$row" ] || continue
            id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row")
            rc=0
            (cd "$T/root-$p/repo" && jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}' \
                | env -u TMPDIR LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 LOA_REPO_ROOT="$T/root-$p" LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" \
                  bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
            echo "$id $rc" >> "$T/fence-$p.txt"
        done < "$T/all.jsonl"
    done
    cmp "$T/fence-lean.txt" "$T/fence-standard.txt"
    for id in FP-1 FP-2 FP-3 FP-4 FP-5; do
        grep -qx "$id 2" "$T/fence-lean.txt" || { echo "$id not blocked under lean: $(grep "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt")"; return 1; }
    done
    # Every floor_corpus row present in the corpus is in the compared set.
    while IFS= read -r rule; do
        jq -r --arg r "$rule" 'select(.rule == $r or (($r | endswith("*")) and (.rule | startswith($r | rtrimstr("*"))))) | .id' \
            "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" | while IFS= read -r id; do
            grep -q "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt"
        done
    done < <(yq -r '.floor_corpus.rules[]' "$FLOOR")
}

@test "PF-7 the deny list, the System-Zone rules and user-invoked-commands.txt are untouched by resolving any profile" {
    local f before after p
    for f in .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt .claude/rules/zone-system.md .claude/data/floor.yaml; do
        before=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
        for p in lean standard; do
            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/cache-$p.json" bash "$LIB" json >/dev/null
        done
        after=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
        [ "$before" = "$after" ]
    done
    # The lib reads exactly three inputs and writes only its cache.
    ! grep -Eq 'settings\.deny|user-invoked-commands|zone-system' "$LIB"
    # The resolved documents differ only in the profile name and the profile-sourced values.
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "lean" ]
    [ "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-standard.json")" ]
}

([$tn, ($lines | tostring), ($now | todate), ($file | tojson),
                ($session | tojson), ($files_mod | tostring), ($tool_calls | tostring)]
               | join($z) + $z)
            ) catch ("__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" + $z)
          ' 2>/dev/null || _jrc=$?
          printf '%s' "$_jrc"
        }
    )
    [[ "${#_kf[@]}" -ge 1 ]] || exit 0
    _jqrc="${_kf[-1]}"
    # Invalid JSON on stdin — the old `jq empty 2>/dev/null || exit 0` path.
    [[ "$_jqrc" == "0" ]] || exit 0
    # Post-validation extraction error — the old unguarded-extraction set -e
    # death (pipefail propagated jq's exit code 5).
    if [[ "${#_kf[@]}" -eq 2 && "${_kf[0]}" == "__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" ]]; then
        exit 5
    fi
    [[ "${#_kf[@]}" -eq 8 ]] || exit 0  # defensive: unexpected field count

    TOOL_NAME="${_kf[0]}"
    LINES="${_kf[1]}"
    TS="${_kf[2]}"
    FILE_JSON="${_kf[3]}"
    SESSION_JSON="${_kf[4]}"
    FILES_MOD="${_kf[5]}"
    TOOL_CALLS="${_kf[6]}"
fi

[[ -n "$TOOL_NAME" ]] || exit 0

# Tool dispatch. Lines were computed for the matching shape inside jq
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string — conservative, counts
# new content only; the v1 simplification documented in SDD §0.3).
case "$TOOL_NAME" in
    Write|Edit|NotebookEdit)
        ;;
    *)
        # Unrecognized tool — no-op (defensive: settings.json matcher should
        # prevent this, but the hook stays safe even if matcher widens).
        exit 0
        ;;
esac

[[ "$LINES" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 0

# perf pass-4: skip the dirname+mkdir spawns when the parent dir already
# exists (the steady state). The guard passing proves dirname's target
# exists (e.g. "a/b" being a dir ⇒ "a" exists), so mkdir -p would be a
# no-op; every other shape (no slash, trailing slash, missing parent) takes
# the old command unchanged.
if [[ "${TASK_STATE%/*}" == "$TASK_STATE" || ! -d "${TASK_STATE%/*}" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TASK_STATE")"
fi

# Running total: sum lines_changed across existing state entries + this call.
# Awk parse is intentionally tolerant of malformed lines (skips them).
# perf pass-7: FAST serves the cached total (== the full scan's printed
# value: cache writes require an exact-decimal 15-digit integer); DELTA
# re-runs THE SAME awk program on only the token+delta bytes, seeded with
# the cached total in BEGIN — same association order as the full scan.
if [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "fast" ]]; then
    RUNNING="$_kp7_bsum"
elif [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
    RUNNING=$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' -v init="$_kp7_bsum" '
        BEGIN { sum = init + 0 }
        NR == 1 { next }
        /"lines_changed":/ {
            n = $2 + 0  # extract leading integer
            sum += n
        }
        END { print sum + 0 }
    ' <(tail -c +"$_kp7_tail_from" -- "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
else
    RUNNING=$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '
        /"lines_changed":/ {
            n = $2 + 0  # extract leading integer
            sum += n
        }
        END { print sum + 0 }
    ' "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
fi
RUNNING=$((RUNNING + LINES))

# Append entry to state — printf-assembled from jq-pre-encoded pieces;
# byte-identical to the old jq -nc output (see header note).
# perf pass-7: the line is built in a variable first (printf -v cannot
# fail; identical bytes) so it can double as the cache's prefix-integrity
# token; the append keeps the old failure shape.
printf -v _kp7_entry '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s}' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON"
printf '%s\n' "$_kp7_entry" >> "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Threshold check.
if (( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )); then
    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_STATE" >&2

    # Trajectory event (#961 K-2 FR-3 schema).
    # perf pass-4: [[ -d ]] guard — mkdir -p only when the dir is missing.
    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR"
    TRAJ_FILE="$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl"
    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0

    # A leading-zero THRESHOLD (e.g. config "007") passed the ^[0-9]+$ guard;
    # the old `jq -nc --argjson thresh "007"` PARSED it leniently and wrote
    # the decimal-normalized number (007 -> 7) — corpus-verified. Replicate
    # with a textual leading-zero strip (identical to jq's integer rendering
    # for every warn-reachable threshold).
    THRESHOLD_JSON="$THRESHOLD"
    while [[ "$THRESHOLD_JSON" == 0?* ]]; do THRESHOLD_JSON="${THRESHOLD_JSON#0}"; done

    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD_JSON" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

I found two real logic defects in the reworked hook, plus a latency regression and some stale wording. Everything is attributable to the head version.

**Setup.** I copied `pr/head` to `~/rv2`. `/tmp` is mounted noexec, so the bats `[[ -x "$HOOK" ]]` guard would have skipped every test there. I also fixed a redaction artifact that stops `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats` from parsing: `local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"` appears in both the base and head snapshots, so it isn't a PR defect. All 21 tests in the three bats files then pass.

### 1. The counter is keyed on the previous task, not the current one (high)
**Where:** `.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh` lines 10–12 (header comment) and lines 129–136 (code).
- The hook takes `.checkpoint.task` from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`.
- `read` only returns a checkpoint whose bead `br` reports **closed**; an open bead's checkpoint is discarded (`run-checkpoint.sh` lines 187–211).
- The checkpoint is only written after `br close` (`implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:211`), and `run-mode/resources/state-schemas.md:107` says "`task` is the last CLOSED bead".
- So the task currently being worked on is never the key. Task 1's lines go into `<sprint>.jsonl`, task 2's lines go into `bd-1.jsonl`, and so on.
- The summary's `.task` and the per-bead files are mislabelled by one task. `reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220` has the SURGICAL axis read `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl`, so it gets the wrong task's data.
- The tests hide this: `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats` setup (lines 31–33) uses a fake `br` that reports every bead closed, so KS-1 acts as if the checkpoint names the in-progress task, which never happens in a real run.

**How verified:** I ran the real `run-checkpoint.sh write` flow with a stateful fake `br`:
- Before any task closed, with checkpoint `sprint-1`, I wrote 10 lines for bd-1. They landed in `sprint-1.jsonl`.
- After `br close bd-1` and `write --task bd-1`, I wrote 30 lines for bd-2. The summary showed `{"task":"bd-1","lines":30}` and `bd-1.jsonl` had `running_total` 30.
- After closing bd-2, I wrote 7 lines for bd-3. They landed in `bd-2.jsonl`.

### 2. A finished or halted run's checkpoint keys every later session (medium)
**Where:** same file, lines 129–138 (and the "else the session id" claim at line 11; the bats setup comments say "with no run in progress … the key is the session id").
- The hook never checks that a run is actually in progress (`.state == RUNNING`).
- `sprint-plan-state.json` is not deleted when a run ends (grep found no remover).
- So after a run reaches JACKED_OUT, every later interactive session keeps adding to the old last-closed-task file. The counter never resets and the session-id fallback never happens.

**How verified:** with a fixture `{state:"JACKED_OUT", checkpoint:{sprint:"sprint-250", task:"bd-old"}}`, Writes from `session_id` sessA and then sessB both went into `bd-old.jsonl`. The total reached 6, the summary said `task:"bd-old"`, and the warning fired.

### 3. Per-write latency is about 6–14x higher (medium, perf)
**Where:** same file, lines 70–80 and 129–135.
- Every Write/Edit now sources `profile-lib.sh` and calls `loa_knob` twice. `diff_lines_per_task` is not a profile key, so it always falls through to a live `yq` read (`profile-lib.sh` `_loa_pl_live`).
- It also runs `bash run-checkpoint.sh read --json` (about six `jq` calls plus a `br show`).
- The header's design note (lines 40–44) says only the unbounded state file needed the old perf work. That ignores these new costs.

**How verified:** timed 10 calls on this host, with the default config and a warm profile cache:

| Version | Per write |
|---|---|
| Base | ~24 ms |
| Head, no run state | ~145 ms |
| Head, run checkpoint present | ~380 ms (seam config) |
| Head, knob off | ~22 ms (the example config's "<10ms" claim no longer holds) |

### 4. Wording that contradicts the per-task design (low)
- `karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:193`: the warning still says "Session diff total …". KS-4 (`karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:89`) pins that wording on purpose, but it now reports a per-task total.
- `.loa.config.yaml.example:2934–2936` still calls the threshold "per-session" and refers to "the session accumulator". This section was not updated.
- `tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff-hook.bats:7`: the header still says "session diff accumulator".

### 5. `profile-lib.sh` cache key breaks on Linux when an input file is missing (low; the hook's normal path doesn't hit it)
**Where:** `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh` lines 76–78.
- If any of config, `profiles.yaml` or `floor.yaml` is missing, GNU `stat -Lc` fails, and the macOS-style fallback `stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z'` runs.
- On GNU, `-f` means "filesystem status", so the cache ID becomes filesystem free-space statistics instead of the files' mtime and size. Cache invalidation then depends on disk usage rather than file edits.

**How verified:** ran that exact pipeline with one missing file; the result held the multi-line filesystem stat output.

### Checked and found correct
- The master switch through `loa_knob`: an explicit `false` is honoured (no `//` problem), and `lean` with no key turns the hook off while an explicit `true` wins.
- The threshold check.
- Exit codes are always 0; the base's exit 5 for a non-object payload is gone, which is an improvement.
- No tool content leaks into state, summary or trajectory.
- Key sanitising and symlink guards.
- Keeping only 20 state files.
- The trajectory event has the same field set as base.
- No bash 3.2 constructs that break.

**Already in base, not introduced by this PR:** NotebookEdit payloads carry `notebook_path` and `new_source`, but the hook reads `file_path` and `new_string`. So NotebookEdit always counts 0 lines and the file is logged as `<unknown>`, even though the head header says it is counted (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh` lines 6–7 and 92–94).

# tests/unit/prompt-audit-keeplist.bats — cycle-124 FR-8 / AC-8.3
#
# tools/prompt-keeplist.txt names the prompt text the audit may never delete
# (fences and remedies, the one-way verdict rule, the zone model, tool
# contracts, format-pinning examples, agent-network invariants, routing text,
# the list itself). Each entry is `<id> TAB <glob> TAB <ERE> TAB <reason>`;
# every file the glob matches must still match the ERE, and the human
# companion tools/prompt-keeplist.md explains
# every id.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    LIST="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/prompt-keeplist.txt"
    COMPANION="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/prompt-keeplist.md"
}

entries() { grep -v -E '^\s*(#|$)' "$LIST"; }

@test "KL-1 every entry has four tab-separated fields, a unique K-NN id and a reason" {
    local n ids
    n="$(entries | awk -F'\t' 'NF!=4 || $1 !~ /^K-[0-9]{2}$/ || $4 == ""' | wc -l)"
    [ "$n" -eq 0 ]
    ids="$(entries | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -d)"
    [ -z "$ids" ]
    [ "$(entries | wc -l)" -ge 40 ]
}

@test "KL-2 every keep-listed string survives in every file its glob matches" {
    local failures=0 id glob ere reason f matched
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r id glob ere reason; do
        matched=0
        shopt -s nullglob
        # brace lists and globs expand relative to the repo root
        for f in $(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && eval "printf '%s\n' $glob"); do
            matched=1
            if ! grep -qE -- "$ere" "$PROJECT_ROOT/$f"; then
                echo "MISSING $id in $f: /$ere/ ($reason)"
                failures=$((failures + 1))
            fi
        done
        shopt -u nullglob
        if [ "$matched" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "NO FILE for $id glob $glob"
            failures=$((failures + 1))
        fi
    done < <(entries)
    [ "$failures" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "KL-3 the companion keep-list.md explains every id" {
    [ -f "$COMPANION" ]
    local missing=0 id rest
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r id rest; do
        grep -q -- "$id" "$COMPANION" || { echo "no companion row for $id"; missing=$((missing + 1)); }
    done < <(entries)
    [ "$missing" -eq 0 ]

## Phase -2: Beads-First Integration

### Task Tracking: Beads vs TaskCreate

Use `br` (beads_rust) exclusively for sprint task lifecycle (commands below). Claude's `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` are for session-level progress display only; tasks tracked only there are invisible to cross-session recovery, `/run-resume`, and beads health checks.

```bash
health=$(.claude/scripts/beads/beads-health.sh --quick --json)
status=$(echo "$health" | jq -r '.status')
```

`HEALTHY` → import state (`br sync --import-only`; `update-beads-state.sh --sync-import`) and proceed. `DEGRADED` → warn, import, proceed. `NOT_INSTALLED`/`NOT_INITIALIZED` → check opt-out (`update-beads-state.sh --opt-out-check`); without one, warn (`cargo install beads_rust && br init` to add it) and fall back to markdown. `MIGRATION_NEEDED`/`UNHEALTHY` → warn, fall back to markdown. Record the outcome: `.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh --health "$status"`.

Run the full lifecycle per task yourself: health check → `br sync --import-only` → `.claude/scripts/beads/get-ready-work.sh` (not bare `br ready`) → `br update <id> --status in_progress` → implement → `br close <id>` (run mode: then `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --task <id> --phase IMPLEMENT`) → `br sync --flush-only` at session end. Log discovered issues as they surface — this adds a `discovered-during:<parent-id>` label for traceability:

```bash
.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh "$CURRENT_TASK_ID" "Description of discovered issue" bug 2
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
# DEC-0141).
#
# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
# PER TASK:
#
#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}
payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"

task_raw=""
if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
fi
KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"

# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi

# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2

    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |

content.text:
I found nine defects in the `loa.profile` lib and its readers: one high, three medium, five low. Every one was reproduced in a scratch copy of `pr/head` at `/tmp/rv3` (yq is mikefarah v4.40.5 at `/usr/local/bin/yq`; jq and bats 1.13 are also present).

Things I checked that hold up:
- **Precedence:** explicit key, then profile, then fallback. An explicit `false` beats a profile `true` (the `getpath` / `!= null` logic is right), and both PL-6 and my own configs pass.
- **Standard values:** the `standard` values match the example and the oracle, and the oracle's base-reader values are accurate.
- **Inlined copies:** the included text in all six SKILL.md files matches the includes byte for byte.
- **Lint:** `tools/check-knob-readers.sh` passes.
- **Guardrail scripts:** they resolve as documented.
- **Portability:** the bash 3.2 constructs are fine.

**Test runs:** in this partial tree, `floor.yaml`, `time-lib.sh` and similar files are missing. With a stub `floor.yaml`, everything in `profile-lib.bats` passes except PL-14 and PL-15, and both of those fail only because of missing dependencies. PF-1 to PF-5 also fail for missing files.

## Findings

**1. HIGH — `loa.profile` does almost nothing on a fresh install.** `.loa.config.yaml.example:33` (`profile: standard`), with the claim at lines 21-23.
- The example sets 8 of the 9 profile keys explicitly: lines 312, 325, 1358, 1404, 1432, 2932, 2950 and 2962. An explicit key always beats the profile.
- So a user who copies the example and changes the profile to `lean` or `full` gets the same value for those 8 keys. Only `soul_identity_doc.enabled` changes.
- The comment "`lean` turns them all off, `full` all on" is false for the file it sits in.
- Verified: I copied the example, set `loa.profile = full` with `yq -i`, and ran `profile-lib.sh json`. 8 knobs show `source: explicit` with the standard values. `overrides` lists 5 keys at `=false`. With `lean`, `surgical_diff_warning`, `require_success_criteria` and `invisible_retrospective` stay `true`.
- Fix: comment those keys out in the example, or ship them unset.

**2. MEDIUM — the cache can go stale on Linux when any input file is missing.** `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77-78`.
- GNU `stat -Lc` exits non-zero if any of config / `profiles.yaml` / `floor.yaml` is missing. The fallback `stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z'` is the BSD form.
- On GNU, `-f` means filesystem status, and the format string is taken as a file name. The cache key then holds filesystem block counts, not file mtime or size, so edits often don't invalidate it.
- The "empty stat output disables caching" guard at line 79 doesn't catch this.
- Verified: with no `floor.yaml`, I wrote `profile: lean`, ran `knob`, then rewrote the config to `profile: full`. Both `knob` and `profile` still return the lean values. With `floor.yaml` present the profile is picked up. This is also why PL-5 and PL-8 failed until I stubbed `floor.yaml`.
- Fix: don't treat partial output as failure, or pick the stat flavour by probing `stat --version`.

**3. MEDIUM — the session-start surfaces now silently need jq.**
- Files: `.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh:63-64`, `.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh:50-51`, `.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-l7-surface-soul.sh:69-75`.
- `loa_knob` needs jq, and so does its fallback reader `_loa_pl_live` (lib lines 208-209). Without jq it returns the fallback (`false`) even for an explicit `true`.
- The KF and L7 hooks never needed jq before; base read the key with yq alone. Now an enabled surface goes silent.
- The decisions hook's documented contract (header lines 12-13) is "enabled but jq missing → one WARNING line". It now prints nothing.
- Verified: with jq removed from PATH, the base KF hook prints `[KF-SURFACE] WARNING…` and the head hook prints nothing. With `decisions.surface_at_session_start: true`, base prints `[DECISIONS] WARNING … jq is missing` and head prints nothing, exit 0.
- Related: the decisions hook's no-yq awk fallback (lines 53-57) ignores the profile entirely.

**4. MEDIUM — the invisible retrospective now runs by default where it used to be off.**
- Files: `.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` (and the inlined copies at `auditing-security/SKILL.md:285`, `implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:244`, `reviewing-code/SKILL.md:297`), plus `profiles.yaml:42`.
- Base ran the scan only on an explicit `true`. Head runs it when the key is absent, because `standard` is `true`.
- This repo's `.loa.config.yaml` has no `invisible_retrospective` key, so it flips from off to on here. The oracle itself records `this_repo_today: false`.
- The PR protects this repo's guardrail behaviour with explicit keys and calls that "a migration item", but does nothing similar for the retrospective.
- Verified: in `/tmp/rv3`, `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` prints `true`, while `yq '.invisible_retrospective'` on the base config is `null`.

**5. LOW-MEDIUM — the lib's override env vars work in production, not just under bats.** `profile-lib.sh:51,61-65`.
- `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILES_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_ROOT` and `LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE` are honoured with no bats gate. Only `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` is gated.
- That breaks the hooks' stated rule that overrides are honoured only under bats (`loa-kf-surface.sh:39-41`). It also lets an env var redirect `guardrails.danger_level.enforce` and `guardrails.input.enabled`.
- Verified: with no bats variables set, `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE=/tmp/off.yaml bash .claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh` suppresses a surface that the repo config enables.

**6. LOW — a config with more than one YAML document breaks resolution.** `profile-lib.sh:96,115`.
- `yq -o=json '.'` prints one JSON document per YAML document, and `jq -s` then gets the inputs out of order: the config's second document lands where the profiles should be.
- Verified: a config of `---\nloa:\n  profile: full\n---\n` gives `profile_keys: []` and the warning `unknown loa.profile "full"`.
- Fix: read only the first document, e.g. `select(document_index==0)`.

**7. LOW — the floor check misses a profile key nested under a non-wildcard floor key.** `profile-lib.sh:124`, with the same gap in `tests/unit/profile-floor.bats:57-58`.
- `forbidden()` blocks exact and glob matches and parent keys, but not child keys. With `floor_keys: [hounfour.locality]`, a profile key `hounfour.locality.mode` is still applied.
- Verified: `knob hounfour.locality.mode local` returns the profile value `remote`.

**8. LOW — `run-mode` still uses the old guardrails rule, and the lint can't see it.** `.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:26`.
- The old text "Skip … when `guardrails.input.enabled: false`" is unchanged, so an absent key means run.
- `check-knob-readers.sh` only flags key paths with a leading dot, so this prose passes.
- Impact is small: the orchestrator now checks the knob itself and returns `PROCEED "guardrails disabled in config"`.

**9. LOW — the docs disagree on the `knob` fallback argument.**
- `profile-lib.sh:10,19` documents `knob <path> <fallback>`, but the CLI at line 302 treats the fallback as optional.
- `retrospective_postlude.md:1` passes no fallback, so it reads empty and the scan is off when jq or yq is missing.
- `continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34` documents the same call with fallback `true`, which gives the opposite degraded behaviour.

## Test-quality note
In the full tree, PL-5 and PL-8 pass only because all three input files exist. They never exercise the missing-file path from finding 2. PL-16 depends on the ungated seam from finding 5.

name: Prompt Budget

# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1): the always-loaded prompt surface has hard byte
# budgets — SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read resources),
# CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn > 114,688 B).
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh is the gate; the two sentinel steps prove the
# gate itself still bites (a scanner that exits 0 from a syntax error must not
# read as green).

on:
  # Every pull request: the gate takes seconds, and a path filter would miss the
  # shared inputs the checker charges (skill includes rendered into SKILL.md,
  # resources read unconditionally, the keep list) — Bridgebuilder F-001 on
  # PR #1266.
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  prompt-budget:
    name: Byte budgets for the prompt surface
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5

      - name: Check budgets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json > prompt-budget.json || rc=$?
          # A checker that dies before writing a report must fail LOUD with its
          # exit code, not as an opaque jq parse error (Bridgebuilder F-003).
          if ! jq -e . prompt-budget.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh --json produced no parseable report (exit $rc)"
            cat prompt-budget.json || true
            exit 1
          fi
          # Human-readable table for the log; the JSON gate below is the verdict.
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh || echo "::notice::human-readable run exited non-zero; the JSON gate decides"
          jq -r '.violations[]? | "::error::prompt budget: \(.)"' prompt-budget.json
          jq -e '.ok' prompt-budget.json >/dev/null

      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the over-budget sentinel with exit 1)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over --quiet || rc=$?
          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh did not reject tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over with exit 1 (got $rc)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: over-budget sentinel rejected"

      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the under-budget sentinel)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under --quiet; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh false-positive on tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: under-budget sentinel accepted"

      - name: Upload report
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: prompt-budget-report
          path: prompt-budget.json
          retention-days: 14

check_constraint_blocks() {
  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "CLAUDE.loa.md not found"
    return
  fi

  local block_count
  block_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$block_count" ]] && block_count=0

  if [[ "$block_count" -ge 3 ]]; then
    report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "$block_count constraint-generated blocks found"
  elif [[ "$block_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraint-blocks" "Only $block_count constraint-generated blocks (expected 3+)"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "No constraint-generated blocks found"
  fi

  # Check start/end pairs match
  local start_count end_count
  start_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  end_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: end' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$start_count" ]] && start_count=0
  [[ -z "$end_count" ]] && end_count=0

  if [[ "$start_count" -ne "$end_count" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "Mismatched start/end pairs: $start_count starts, $end_count ends"
  fi
}
