content.text:
I found seven defects in my scope. Four are fail-open bypasses: commands the base hook blocks are now allowed under the default config (`heredoc_classifier: true`), and I ran three of them in real bash and watched them do damage. I built each finding concretely: I copied head and base to `/tmp/rv1`, piped each command to both hooks as `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":...}}` JSON, ran the classifier through `lib/heredoc-classifier.sh`, and ran the corpus runner under the default, `--knob-off` and `--hook <base>`. Paths are relative to `pr/head/`.

## Findings

**1. CRLF folding makes the classifier disagree with bash about where a heredoc ends (fail-open)**
- **Where:** `.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:647` (`text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"`), with the terminator search at 669–673.
- **Problem:** the classifier folds CRLF to LF before it looks for the terminator, but bash does not fold. A line `EOF\r` therefore closes the heredoc for the classifier and not for bash. That lets an attacker plant a second, fake header inside what bash still treats as body. The fake heredoc's "body" is then really live shell, and any segment whose first word is not in the short fence-verb list gets dropped.
- **Command:** `cat > a.md <<'EOF'` / `EOF\r` / `cat > b.md <<'X'` / `EOF` / `cp evil .claude/settings.json` / `X`
- **Result:** base exits 2 (FR-SZ2-COPY). Head exits 0 and the class is `nonexec`. Running it with `bash -c` really wrote `.claude/settings.json`. A variant with `\r` on the header instead of the terminator behaves the same way.
- **Docs:** `hooks-reference.md:293` presents CRLF folding as part of the grammar, with no caveat.

**2. Backslash-newline in an unquoted heredoc body has the same effect (fail-open)**
- **Where:** `block-destructive-bash.sh:669–673` and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (lines 576–583).
- **Problem:** with an unquoted delimiter, bash joins a body line ending in `\` to the next line, so `x\` followed by `EOF` becomes the body text `xEOF` and does not close the heredoc. The classifier closes it at that `EOF`.
- **Command:** `cat > a.md <<EOF` / `x\` / `EOF` / `cat > b.md <<'X'` / `EOF` / `if :; then rm -rf src; fi` / `X`
- **Result:** base exits 2 (FR-2-AMBIGUOUS). Head exits 0. Running it in bash really deleted `src/`.

**3. The same-command execution check is trivially evaded (fail-open)**
- **Where:** `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`, lines 608–641. It looks for the target's literal basename as a substring or token elsewhere in the command.
- **Problem:** the target can be run without its literal name appearing. Each of these gives base exit 2 and head exit 0, class `nonexec`:
  - `cat > x.md <<'EOF'` / `cp evil .claude/settings.json` / `EOF` / `bash x.m"d"` (quoting)
  - the same with `bash ./x.*` (glob)
  - `f=x.md; bash $f` (the target goes through a variable, so its name never appears as its own token)

content.text:
I found no high-severity defects in the scoped files. There are four real but low-severity issues, listed below.

**How I checked:** `/tmp` is mounted noexec, so I worked in `$HOME`. I cloned upstream `0xHoneyJar/loa` main, which already contains this PR (40 of the 57 touched files there are byte-identical to `head/`). I copied `pr/head` over it to get a runnable tree. In that tree:
- `generate-constraints.sh --dry-run` shows no drift.
- `validate-constraints.sh` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `test-lint-invariants.sh` passes 18/18.
- `check-prompt-budget.sh` passes: CLAUDE.loa.md is 9189 B against the 9445 B cap, and both CI sentinel fixtures still behave correctly.
- The full validator run (`validate-skill-capabilities.sh`) passes all 37 skills, so no other pure-review skill trips the new ERROR.
- These bats files all pass: `lint-invariants`, `prompt-budget`, `instruction-diet-revert`, `skill-capabilities` (the c129 tests), `golden-path-c8-verdict-trailer`, `prompt-audit-generated-blocks`, `skill-includes`, `bug-989-kernel-hash-stamp`, `agent-teams-hooks`. Two cases fail, SC-T-AGENT-7 and "non-integer review excluded", but they fail the same way on unmodified upstream, so they are environment failures, not this PR.

## Findings

1. **`.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh:142` (with the new SECTIONS row at :27 and the comment at :35-40)**
   - **Problem:** When `agent_teams_constraints` rows exist but the kernel has no markers, the error tells you to "Run with --bootstrap --confirm to insert." But `agent_teams_constraints` has no entry in `ANCHORS` (:209-217), so bootstrap does nothing. It prints `WARNING: No anchor defined ... skipping`, re-stamps the `@loa-managed` hash, logs "Generation complete: 1 target(s) updated" and exits 0, with nothing inserted. The fix it suggests is a silent no-op. The header comment admits bootstrap can't re-create the heading, but the error message still points there.
   - **Verified:** On a fixture holding a C-TEAM-901 row, normal generation exits 1 with "Missing markers". `--bootstrap --confirm` then exits 0, and `grep -c agent_teams` on the kernel is still 0.

2. **`.claude/scripts/validate-constraints.sh:25` (new row) together with `check_section_freshness` (around :355-358)**
   - **Problem:** If agent_teams rows come back but the kernel has no block, the freshness check skips the section quietly (only a verbose log line) and the validator passes. Only the new lint invariant (`lint-invariants.sh:229-250`) catches it. The skip-when-no-markers behaviour is old, but the new optional section is exactly the case where it hides a real gap: generate fails while validate passes.
   - **Verified:** By reading the code. The same fixture shows the generator failing, and the validator has no check for rows that never got rendered.

3. **`.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1-2`, which renders into `.claude/skills/{auditing-security,implementing-tasks,reviewing-code}/SKILL.md`, compared with `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34`**
   - **Problem:** The two docs give different fallbacks. The include calls `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback; the resource doc says `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`. When profiles can't be resolved (profiles.yaml missing, or no yq/jq), the include path prints an empty string, so the retrospective is skipped. The resource doc's version prints `true`, so it runs. Compare `input_guardrails.md`, which passes its fallback (`false`) consistently in both places.
   - **Verified:** With `LOA_PROFILES_FILE=/nonexistent`, `knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` prints an empty line, while adding `true` prints `true`.

4. **`.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:133`**
   - **Problem:** It says the thresholds live in "that file and `run_mode.defaults`". In `run-checkpoint.sh:488-491`, `run_mode.defaults` only supplies `max_cycles` and `timeout_hours`. The same-issue and no-progress thresholds come from `run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold`. The prose that replaced the old table points readers at the wrong config key for two of the four triggers.
   - **Verified:** Compared the doc against the script's `cfg_int` calls.

## Checked and fine
- **C-TEAM leftovers:**
  - No head file still expects C-TEAM rows in `constraints.json`.
  - The remaining C-TEAM mentions are deliberate ID names: in the team hooks, in agent-teams-reference, and in the K-07 entry in `tools/prompt-keeplist.md`.
  - CLAUDE.loa.md has no `agent_teams_constraints` marker and no `## Agent Teams` heading, and its `@loa-managed` hash verifies.
- **Prune logic in `generate-constraints.sh`:**
  - Applied to the base kernel, pruning gives exactly the head kernel (only the hash line differs) and is idempotent.
  - It errors correctly on foreign prose above the table, on a missing end marker, and on a missing heading.
- **Rationales moved to agent-teams-reference:** All five C-TEAM rationales there match the base `constraints.json` `why` strings exactly, so IDR-3 is valid.
- **`validate-skill-capabilities.sh` pure-review check:**
  - The yq expression handles both the list form and the comma-string form.
  - `grep -w` does not mistake "NotebookEdit" for "Edit".
  - `rtfm-testing` matches by directory name, so the exceptions list works.
- **Doc flags against `run-checkpoint.sh`'s CLI:** Every invocation in the skills uses subcommands and flags the script accepts: `write`/`--phase IMPLEMENT`, `mark --skill implement|bug`, `record-round --gate --file --sprint`, `derive --json|--write`, and the `.drift`/`.cache_state` fields.
- **Test change in `test-lint-invariants.sh:254,320`:** The good-fixture assertion was relaxed from exit 0 to "0 or 1". That is justified: base already failed it with exit 1 because of environment WARNs.
- **Bash 3.2:** The new code adds nothing new to worry about. `generate-constraints.sh` already used `declare -A` behind its version guard.

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:647 — Fail-open. The classifier folds CRLF to LF before it looks for the heredoc terminator; bash does not. A line `EOF\r` therefore closes the heredoc for the classifier but not for bash, and a fake second header planted in the still-open body turns live shell into "nonexec" body. Reproduced: `cat > a.md <<'EOF'` / `EOF\r` / `cat > b.md <<'X'` / `EOF` / `cp evil .claude/settings.json` / `X`: base exits 2 (FR-SZ2-COPY), head exits 0, and bash really writes .claude/settings.json. hooks-reference.md:293 documents the folding with no caveat.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:672 — Fail-open. The terminator search ignores backslash-newline joining in unquoted-delimiter bodies: in bash, `x\` followed by `EOF` is the body text `xEOF`, but the classifier closes the heredoc at that `EOF`. Same fake-header trick: `cat > a.md <<EOF` / `x\` / `EOF` / `cat > b.md <<'X'` / `EOF` / `if :; then rm -rf src; fi` / `X`: base exits 2 (FR-2-AMBIGUOUS), head exits 0, and bash deletes src/.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:546 — `_bdb_hd_segword` does not strip the shell keywords `then`, `do`, `else` and `elif`, so a fence verb after one of them is dropped from the per-segment body scan. That contradicts the rule that a fence-verb segment stays visible. Reproduced: `tee n.md <<'EOF'` / `if :; then git push --force origin main; fi` / `EOF`: base exits 2 (P2), head exits 0.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608 — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` only detects that the heredoc target gets executed if the target's literal basename appears in the command. Quoting (`bash x.m"d"`), a glob (`bash ./x.*`), a variable (`f=x.md; bash $f`) and `exec > x.sh` followed by a bare `cat <<'EOF'` all evade it, so the body is classified nonexec: base blocks, head allows. Also, the executable-destination list at line 190 omits Makefile, package.json, .github/workflows and similar, so `cat > Makefile <<'EOF' … EOF; make` is allowed.

The PR can't merge: **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. `review.md` at the repository root lists 26 findings, each as `head/<path>:<line> — …`. Nothing under `pr/` was modified.

**Blocking problems, each reproduced against the head files:**

- **The heredoc classifier lets dangerous commands through.** The PR describes it as fail-closed, but with the default `heredoc_classifier: true` several commands the base hook blocks are now allowed. In each case base exits 2 (blocked) and head exits 0 (allowed):
  - A line ending in `EOF\r` closes the heredoc for the classifier but not for bash. That let `cp evil .claude/settings.json` run (`block-destructive-bash.sh:647`).
  - A trailing backslash joins the next line in bash, so the classifier and bash disagree about where the heredoc ends. That let `rm -rf src` run (`:672`).
  - `then git push --force …` inside a `tee` heredoc is ignored, because words like `then` and `do` aren't stripped before the command word is checked (`:546`).
  - The check for whether the heredoc's target file gets executed only looks for the file's literal name. Quoting part of the name, a glob, a variable, or writing a `Makefile` and running `make` all get past it (`:608`, `:190`).
  - The config comment says turning the classifier off "only tightens". It doesn't: six dangerous corpus rows pass with it off.
- **`run-checkpoint.sh derive` doesn't work on jq 1.6.** It uses a jq variable named `$label`, which jq 1.6 rejects as a syntax error. Every `write` and `mark` calls derive, so on jq 1.6 the run-position cache never refreshes (`:380`). jq 1.6 also breaks the handling of feedback files with no verdict trailer (`:226`).
- **derive halts runs that are going fine.** Feedback files with no verdict trailer always count as failed rounds, and when they have no findings section they all get the same hash. Three plain "All good" approvals trip the breaker and the run is rewritten to HALTED (`:280`).
- **A breaker file created by derive is missing its thresholds and start time,** so the timeout trigger can never fire (`:456`).
- **The surgical-diff counter credits each task's lines to the previous task.** It keys on the last *closed* bead, so the review's SURGICAL check reads the wrong task's numbers (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131`).
- **Switching `loa.profile` does almost nothing for anyone who starts from the example config.** The example sets 8 of the 9 profile keys explicitly, and an explicit key beats the profile (`.loa.config.yaml.example:33`).

The rest are medium or low:
- profile-lib can serve stale cached values on Linux when an input file is missing.
- The session-start messages now go quiet without jq instead of printing a warning.
- The retrospective now runs by default in this repo, where it used to be off.
- The new heredoc library has no caller, and the test credited to it passes without it.
- Assorted doc mismatches, and some corpus rows record a real spike merge and force-push as harmless.

**How it was checked:**
- I reviewed implement-gate and run-checkpoint myself. Four parallel reviewers took the other areas, and I re-ran the key reproductions myself: the jq 1.6 failure, the false HALTED, the incomplete breaker, two of the heredoc bypasses, and the profile/config values.
- implement-gate.bats: all the new cases pass. A few older cases fail because their fixtures aren't in the frozen snapshot.
- Some other suites can't run here because they need files outside the PR, so findings in those areas come from direct runs and code reading.

One of the reviewers cloned the public upstream repository (read-only) to get a runnable tree. With it, generate-constraints, validate-constraints and the lint self-tests all ran clean.
